newsitem.title: INDIA: India court rejects politician's bail application.
newsitem.headline: India court rejects politician's bail application.

text.p: An Indian court on Thursday rejected an application by a powerful politician charged in a $280 million corruption scandal case for "anticipatory bail" to avert arrest by federal police.

A judge in the city of Patna rejected the application by Laloo Prasad Yadav, chief minister of the eastern state of Bihar, in the corruption case which has sharply divided Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's centre-left coalition government.

"The application for anticipatory bail is rejected," Judge Daljit Singh Dhaliwal told a crowded courtroom in an order that sent the New Delhi stock market's benchmark index crashing by 17.43 points to 883.10 within moments.

Yadav, who earlier this month formed a breakaway group of Gujral's Janata Dal party, has refused to resign after the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) indicted him in the corruption case in which he says he is innocent.
Yadav's stand has sharply divided parties in Gujral's 15-party United Front alliance over whether or not to admit his faction, the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD).

The scandal, which involves the alleged siphoning of animal welfare funds in Bihar, has rattled the minority government because Yadav is a powerful low-caste leader with mass support in his state but is seen hurting the alliance's image nationally.
